title: Introduce flight-reservation scheduler and commitment-tracer
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees while allowing short-lived surges without destabilizing headroom. Current soft-burst banks react too aggressively and produce oscillations across tenants under correlated spikes. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a FlightReservationScheduler (FRS) that staggers short-term reservation windows and softly enforces watermarks to smooth admission; 2) a CommitmentTracer telemetry pipeline that records reservation lifecycles and observed fulfillment ratios for per-tenant SLAs.

Design summary: The FRS implements a lightweight slotting layer that converts burst requests into time-boxed reservations (flights). Each flight carries a requested throughput and an expected duration. The scheduler uses a reservoir smoothing algorithm to allocate flights into the existing warm pool and reserved headroom, prioritizing long-running commitments but allowing short flights to be slotted opportunistically. When capacity is tight, the FRS will downscale newly scheduled flights by an adaptive factor and emit a suggested fallback model variant via routing metadata. The CommitmentTracer is a non-blocking collector that annotates tenant traces with: reservation_id, scheduled_slots, actual_tokens_served, fulfillment_ratio, and backoff_reason if any. This ties directly into console dashboards and alert rules.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler core algorithm and unit tests - [x] Non-blocking telemetry collector + protobuf schema - [x] Integration test for a 200-tenant synthetic workload with correlated spikes - [x] Console dashboard draft panels (PR to redwood-docs coming next) - [x] Graceful rollback path: feature flag + conservative default (disabled for 1 week in prod while we monitor)

Backward compatibility and rollout: The feature is guarded behind runtime.feature.flight_reservations (off by default). Existing reservation APIs are unchanged; the scheduler consumes the same reservation objects and annotates them. If the scheduler rejects a flight due to lack of capacity, it returns an HTTP 429 with a structured JSON payload containing fallback.suggested_variant and fallback.retry_after_seconds. Gradual rollout plan: enable in staging for 48h, then 10% traffic in prod, 50% after verification, full enable.

Benchmarks and results: On a 64-GPU dedicated cluster running our synthetic spike profile, median p95 tail latency for high-priority tenants improved by 18% compared to the current soft-burst bank (from 310ms -> 255ms) while overall average utilization increased by 6%. Worst-case fairness deviation (measured as 95th percentile of per-tenant throughput delta) dropped from 22% to 9%. See commit messages for raw numbers.

Security & audit: CommitmentTracer events are sanitized; only hashed tenant identifiers are emitted in non-prod telemetry. No new secrets introduced.

Related work: Links to Linear tickets: ENG-4982 (autoscaler smoothing follow-up), ENG-5077 (commitment telemetry roadmap). Jira SUP-229 notes an incident where correlated spikes caused cascading warm pool depletions — this PR addresses that class of failure.

Migration notes: Operators can opt-out by setting runtime.feature.flight_reservations=false. If enabled, monitor console -> Reservations -> Tracer Fulfillment panel.

Files changed (high level): additions to autoscaler service, scheduler module, a small change to routing metadata, new telemetry protobufs, and unit/integration tests.

This PR is intentionally conservative: the core algorithm is optimized for predictability and observability over aggressive packing. Future follow-ups will add probabilistic preemption and inter-cluster spillover.
commits:
a1c9f8f: scheduler: add FlightReservationScheduler core and reservoir smoothing algorithm
  - initial implementation of slotting and adaptive downscaling
  - unit tests for reservoir edge cases

b3d2c4a: telemetry: introduce CommitmentTracer proto and non-blocking collector
  - protobuf schema under telemetry/v1/reservation.proto
  - buffer-backed emitter with backpressure safeguards

c7e5f11: integration: synthetic 200-tenant workload and perf harness
  - adds harness and CI profile for correlated spike simulation
  - adds small routing metadata for suggested_variant
review_comments: Evan Brooks (2025-01-13): Can we clarify how the adaptive downscale factor is computed? The math in flight_scheduler.go is hard to follow. Suggest adding a short docstring and a unit test for a degenerate case.
Maya Patel (2025-01-13): Reply: Added docstring and expanded unit tests to cover degenerate reservoir sizes. The formula is now broken into two helper functions with descriptive names.

Lin Zhou (2025-01-15): Regarding telemetry volume: will CommitmentTracer create a high-cardinality explosion during multi-tenant load? We should sample or aggregate before emitting to external pipelines.

Maya Patel (2025-01-15): Reply: CommitmentTracer emits aggregated fulfillment buckets by default and falls back to sampling for debug mode. Added comments and a flagized config (telemetry.commitment_tracer.aggregation=true).

Priya Nair (2025-01-17): Safety question: if FRS schedules flights that cannot be satisfied because of a sudden GPU eviction, do we attempt retries or immediately emit a rejection? Need to ensure we don't double-charge reserved tokens.

Maya Patel (2025-01-17): Reply: On sudden node eviction we mark flights as failed with backoff_reason=node_eviction. We do not re-charge tenant credits; instead we surface a compensation ticket in the console for operator review. Added tests to assert no double-charge behavior.
release_notes: Introduce FlightReservationScheduler: smoother short-term reservations and CommitmentTracer telemetry. Guards behind runtime.feature.flight_reservations. Improves p95 latency for heavy-tenancy spikes; adds observability for reservation fulfillment.
